subject: Compatibility exemption playbook for /v1 model transition
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 10 Jan 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Compatibility exemption playbook for /v1 model transition

Team —

As we prepare to deprecate the /v1/generate endpoint behavior tied to the redwood-alpha-1 tokenizer (planned for 2026-03-01), several enterprise customers have asked for formal exceptions. I want to align product, engineering, and sales on a short playbook so we can:

- Define the criteria for granting an exemption (technical risk, contract/commitment level, migration effort).
- Identify what infra and API surface changes are required to support a compatibility flag.
- Agree a sane timeline and comms plan for affected accounts (e.g., 6-week grace vs. 3-month extension).

Attached: migration-impact-matrix.xlsx (impact by account), and I dropped an initial spec: compat-flag-spec.md.

Please reply with: 1) technical feasibility and estimated scoping (Dev), 2) product recommendation on policy (Laura), and 3) whether Customer Success / Sales should be allowed to approve exceptions directly or escalate to leadership (Monica / Jonas).

Thanks —
Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Director, Product Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Jan 2026 10:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Compatibility exemption playbook for /v1 model transition

Evelyn —

Short answer: feasible with caveats.

What we can do: implement an opt-in query parameter (e.g., ?compat=alpha1) that routes requests to a backwards-compatible tokenizer and sequence normalization path. It requires: 
- ~2 wks of core runtime work (tokenizer integration + tests)
- 1 wk infra change to ensure routing and capacity isolation
- Backfill E2E QA for prompt/response parity (3–4 days)

Constraints / caveats:
- The compat path is ~8–12% slower and increases memory footprint for large batch sizes. We should limit it to dedicated/hosted accounts with reservation or explicit opt-in.
- Long-term maintenance cost: every model update will need regression checks for the compat path.
- If we expose as a public flag, we must document deterministic caveats (e.g., token id differences).

Proposal: ship the compat flag behind a feature gate and treat exemptions as a temporary, contract-bound concession (90 days default). For accounts needing more time, require an internal approval ticket (INF-2034).

I attached a short spec (compat-flag-spec.md) and cost estimate. Happy to sync with QA and SRE.

—Dev
Dev Patel
Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Jan 2026 08:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Compatibility exemption playbook for /v1 model transition

Thanks, Dev. That aligns with my thinking. A couple of product notes: 

1) Policy framing: exemptions should be limited to (a) accounts with legal/regulatory constraints preventing tokenizer changes, (b) high-revenue customers with significant integration cost, or (c) platform partners who host the runtime on-prem.

2) Recommendation on duration: offer a 90-day default extension from deprecation date, with the possibility of one 90-day renewal after leadership review (justification required).

3) Comms: we need a two-stream comms plan — an external customer-facing FAQ + migration guide, and an internal escalation playbook for Sales/CS. Draft external FAQ to be hosted at https://drive.google.com/open?id=example-migration-playbook (link below).

4) Rollout: enable feature-gated compat in our Dedicated offering immediately after engineering sign-off; make hosted availability opt-in by request only.

Next: Monica, can you confirm the operational guardrails (who signs exemption requests) and how Sales should record approvals (CRM or a ticket?).

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Senior Product Manager
From: Paul Santos <paul@acme-analytics.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Contracts <contracts@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Jan 2026 09:18:00 -0500
Subject: RE: Compatibility exemption playbook for /v1 model transition

Evelyn —

Thanks for the heads-up. We rely on the current tokenization for our downstream scoring pipelines; changing token ids will break alignment with our on-prem heuristics. We filed an internal migration ticket but need at least 4 months to validate production metrics end-to-end.

Attached is our exemption request (acme-exemption-request.pdf) that outlines the technical risk and committed timeline. We're prepared to sign a short addendum committing to migrate by 2026-07-01 if you can provide a 6-month extension.

Please let me know what information you need from our engineers.

—Paul
Paul Santos
Head of Platform Engineering
Acme Analytics
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Jan 2026 13:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Compatibility exemption playbook for /v1 model transition

Evelyn / team —

I reviewed Acme's request and the technical notes from Dev. Operationally we can support a small set of time-bound exemptions, but we need: 1) a list of accounts, 2) a contract addendum that limits SLA and security guarantees for the compat path, and 3) explicit funding or commit to cover the additional SRE support.

Timeline I can commit to:
- Week 1 (after approval): Feature-gate coding complete and QA validation in staging.
- Week 2: Canary with 1–2 dedicated customers (Acme can volunteer).
- Week 3: if green, opt-in for approved Dedicated accounts.

If Acme requests 6 months, we should require a leadership-level review and signed addendum (legal + finance). Monica — recommend Sales creates a HubSpot approval and attaches the document; if HubSpot can't hold the addendum, escalate to Legal directly.

Jonas
Jonas Weber
Director, Serving Infrastructure
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Paul Santos <paul@acme-analytics.com>, Contracts <contracts@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Jan 2026 16:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Compatibility exemption playbook for /v1 model transition

Thanks all — quick summary and next steps so Sales/Legal have a single source of truth: 

Decisions agreed:
- We will implement a feature-gated compat flag (compat=alpha1) and ship it behind a feature gate for Dedicated accounts.
- Default exemption duration: 90 days from deprecation (2026-03-01). Extensions (up to 180 total) possible with leadership approval and signed addendum.
- Operational gating: SRE will require dedicated canary windows and an explicit support funding line for each account.

Immediate actions: 
1) Dev (by 2026-01-23): finish compat flag spec and PR for runtime changes (INF-2034).
2) Jonas/SRE (by 2026-01-30): provide canary checklist + cost estimate.
3) Monica/Sales (by 2026-01-20): open HubSpot approval for Acme (ACME-4721) and attach acme-exemption-request.pdf. If HubSpot is insufficient, route to Legal (contracts@redwood.com).
4) Laura/Product (by 2026-01-25): publish external FAQ and internal escalation playbook (link: https://drive.google.com/open?id=example-migration-playbook).

Paul — we can start a canary as early as Feb if you can provision a dedicated test project. Monica will coordinate the paperwork.

I'll own the leadership review if we need to extend beyond 90 days — please tag me in the HubSpot ticket.

Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Director, Product Operations
Redwood Inference
